          Premier League Fixture Difficulty vs Results: Which Teams Have Defied Expectations?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design, Ithiel Piñero / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look back at pre-season expectations for Premier League clubs' first five matches and assess how well they've done relative to the supposed difficulty of their fixture schedules.
Five matchdays is all it takes to dramatically alter perspectives and expectations in the Premier League.

Think back to pre-season, that fantastical time of renewal, hope and excitement. Intrusive thoughts about the campaign ahead barely register for most. Instead, brain power is dedicated to thinking about what could be achieved.
Reality can come at you quickly, however.
The 2026-27 Premier League season may only be in relative infancy, but pre-season already feels like a long time ago now, especially for certain clubs.

A good or bad start isn’t always indicative of what’s to come, though. There can be a whole host of reasons for either, and most won’t be permanent. For instance, fixture difficulty is something you cannot ignore – not every start to the season is equal.
On the eve of 2026-27, we used the Opta Power Rankings to determine which clubs had the easiest and toughest opening schedules.
Now, we can look back on those findings to see how they correlate with the real Premier League table after five matchdays.
Generally, there is a loose correlation between fixture difficulty and the points teams earned across the first five matchdays of the season.
For example, the 10 teams deemed to have the easier schedules averaged 8.2 points, whereas the 10 with the toughest have averaged 5.2. But it’s the extremes that are most interesting to look at.

Manchester City lead the fledgling table, of course, having won their first five games. Considering they came into the season with a fair amount of uncertainty surrounding them due to player churn and Pep Guardiola’s exit, their start to the campaign – on the field at least – couldn’t have gone much better.

But it must be pointed out that, according to the pre-season Opta Power Rankings, they had the second-easiest start with an average opponent rating of 91.4. Their opening slate wasn’t without challenges; beating Manchester United away from home despite having 10 men for over an hour was impressive, though most would’ve expected them to take close to maximum points from Bournemouth (H), Crystal Palace (A), Coventry (H) and Sunderland (H).

Liverpool were deemed to have the easiest schedule (91.2). Nine points from those five games probably left most fans slightly underwhelmed, though we must remember the Power Rankings can’t exactly account for elements like adapting to a managerial change with Andoni Iraola now in the hot seat.
In terms of most disappointing start to the season, Man Utd are certainly up there. The Opta Power Rankings suggested they had the third-easiest schedule, but they’ve amassed just five points.

A Matchday 1 defeat to promoted Hull City was alarming. They did at least follow that up with a 5-2 defeat of Ipswich Town at Old Trafford, but that remains their only victory. Sitting 12th after statistically the third-easiest start is understandably concerning.
Brighton are another of the outliers, but for completely different reasons to Man Utd.

With an opening slate of Aston Villa (H), Chelsea (A), Leeds (H), Coventry (A) and Arsenal (H), any nervousness from supporters would’ve been logical. The Opta Power Rankings assessed that as the fourth-hardest start.
But they took 10 points from those games, including an immensely impressive 3-0 dismantling of the champions in their last game before the international break that left them third in the table.

One caveat is that they have spent more time (87 minutes) this season playing against 10 men than any other club, though in fairness to them, they were at least 2-0 up when Villa and Coventry had a man sent off.
If Brighton have been the story of the season so far, then Hull have at least given them a run for their money.
